item.title: Affirm details new AI tool for merchants
item.description: CEO Max Levchin said the lender is testing technology that allows merchants to perform more advanced testing of promotional financing offers.

item.title: Exclusive: Warren targets narrowed bank risk oversight proposal
item.description: A group of Senate Democratic lawmakers warn proposed rule change would handcuff regulators from stopping risky bank behavior before it causes financial harm.

item.title: Nonbank mortgage companies remain a threat to the financial system
item.description: Two years on from a federal report recommending the creation of a resolution fund to guard against disorderly bankruptcies, concentration among nonbank mortgage companies has only increased. Congress must take action to avoid a crisis.

item.title: Visa takes a fresh crack at China's elusive payments market
item.description: By pairing its real-time transfer app with China's UnionPay card, Visa is pursuing business in the huge country, where shifting regulations create hurdles for outside companies.

item.title: The future of palm payments after Amazon's pullback
item.description: While the e-commerce giant has deemphasized the technology, banks and payment firms are testing the biometric option.

item.title: Fed's Jefferson wary of inflationary pressure from AI
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said in a speech Friday that long-term productivity gains brought on by artificial intelligence could compel the central bank to maintain higher rates to keep prices stable.

item.title: Fed 'skinny accounts' take early heat from crypto, fintechs
item.description: Fintech and crypto groups said in comment letters to the Federal Reserve that the proposed "skinny" master account is too limited and could keep firms dependent on banks. Banking groups asked for more time to comment.

item.title: Prosperity completes second of three Texas M&A deals
item.description: Prosperity Bancshares finalizes the second of three acquisitions it's announced since July; Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation appoints a new chief information security officer for its American operations; Huntington Bancshares, Third Coast Bancshares and Heritage Financial completed acquisitions; and more in this week's banking news roundup.

item.title: Banks gain amid software stock rout, despite credit questions
item.description: Artificial intelligence developments are stoking investor fears about software companies. Banks' limited exposure to the sector and general stability is proving attractive to investors.

item.title: Betterment data breach exposes 1.4 million customers
item.description: Threat group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility for the attack, which reportedly targeted third-party platforms rather than Betterment's own systems.
